draft.title: The energy transition
card: The energy transition is the shift from fossil fuels such as coal, oil and gas to renewable energy such as solar and wind. Renewable sources are replaced by natural processes and release little or no greenhouse gas when they generate power.
The shift creates new jobs in building, installing and maintaining equipment such as solar panels, wind turbines and power lines.
It also brings costs. Coal mines and coal-fired power stations may close, and workers and towns that relied on them can lose jobs and income.
The effects differ from place to place. A sunny or windy region may gain new projects, while a coal mining region may face job losses unless new work is found.
draft.remember: The energy transition brings both gains and costs, and they fall on different places.

a.q: Which statement best describes the energy transition?
opts: A move from fossil fuels to renewable energy sources
A move from coal to oil and gas as main fuels
A plan to recycle materials so they stay in use
A rise in the total amount of energy people use
a.why: The energy transition is the shift away from fossil fuels towards renewables such as solar and wind. Moving from coal to oil or gas is tempting, but those are still fossil fuels, so it is not the transition described here.
a.clue: Think about which energy sources are being replaced and which are replacing them.

b.q: A coal-fired power station in a Hunter Valley town is due to close, while a large solar farm is planned for a sunny inland region. Which outcome is most likely?
opts: The town may lose jobs while the inland region gains them
Both places will gain the same number of new jobs
Neither place will see any change in local employment
The inland region will lose jobs while the town gains them
b.why: Closing a coal-fired station can remove jobs from the town that relied on it, while building and running a solar farm can create jobs where it is built. Equal gains in both places are wrong because the transition affects places differently.
b.clue: Ask who loses work when the station closes and who gains work from the new project.

a.best: A move from fossil fuels to renewable energy sources

b.best: The town may lose jobs while the inland region gains them
